turns.t: Hello, doctor. I know this will sound odd, but I keep feeling like I'm going to black out when I'm standing in queues.
It doesn't sound odd at all, it's something I hear fairly often. Tell me what happens.
I go warm all over, and then the room sort of goes dark at the edges.
Have you actually fainted, or does it pass before that?
I've never actually gone down. I always manage to lean on something or sit.
How often has this happened?
Oh, maybe four or five times. Always in a queue, at the bank or the post office.
Does it happen when you're sitting or walking about?
Never then. Only when I'm standing still for a long time.
Do you feel your heart racing, or any chest pain with it?
A little fluttering, I think, but no pain at all.
Do you drink enough water during the day, do you think? ~
Probably not. I'm usually rushing about and I forget. ~
That's useful. Have you been working long hours recently? ~
Yes, extra shifts. I'm tired, to be honest. ~
I can understand that. Does anyone in your family have heart problems or fainting? ~
My dad was a bit of a fainter, but he lived to eighty-five. ~
That's reassuring. Do you smoke, or drink much coffee?
I don't smoke. Coffee, about four cups a day.
Four is a lot, and it can add to the fluttering. Do you eat breakfast? ~
Not really. A coffee on the way to work. ~
Let me tell you what I think is happening. When you stand still, blood can pool in the legs and your pressure dips for a moment.
So it's not something dangerous? ~
Most of the time it isn't, but I'd like to record your heart tracing to make sure the rhythm is normal.
When would that be? ~
I can arrange it for later this week, at the clinic. It takes about ten minutes. ~
That's fine. ~
In the meantime, drink water through the day and have something to eat in the morning.
I will try. ~
If you're in a queue and start feeling it, shift your weight from foot to foot, or sit down straight away.
Okay, I'll do that. ~
And if you do faint, or get chest pain, come in or call at once.
Understood. Thank you. ~
We'll go over the tracing together once it's done. ~
